Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recording is for claim file purposes. Can you please
state your full name for the record?
A: Yes, I'm the policyholder's driver in this matter, and I'd rather keep my name off the transcript if that's alright.
Q: That's understood. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was stopped at a traffic light on a main road in Pasadena, Texas, in the right-hand lane. The light had been red
for a while and traffic was backed up.
Q: What happened next?
A: The vehicle behind me didn't stop in time. I felt a hard jolt from behind, and my head snapped forward and then
back against the seat.
Q: Did you notice any injuries right away?
A: Not really at first. I was more shaken up. But within an hour my right knee started to swell and it hurt when I put
weight on it. It caught on the dashboard, I think, when I was thrown forward.
Q: Have you seen a doctor since the accident?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the same evening, and they took X-rays and told me to follow up with an
orthopedic specialist. I have an appointment set up for later this week.
Q: Were there any witnesses or a police report filed?
A: An officer came to the scene and wrote up a report. I believe there was a passenger in the other car who saw the
impact, but I didn't get their information.
Q: Are you currently missing any time from work because of the knee?
A: Yes, I've had to take time off since I can't stand for long periods. I'm still working through the details of how much
time that's been.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I want to be sure my knee gets properly evaluated, and I'd appreciate hearing what the next steps are for
my claim.
Q: Understood. Thank you for your cooperation. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
